query: World Bog Snorkelling Championships historical winning/fastest times by year, especially 2023, 2024, 2025 results and Neil Rutter times
answer:
Research complete. Here's a summary of my findings on World Bog Snorkelling Championships fastest times:

## Key Findings

**World Record:** 1:12.35 by Neil Rutter (27 Aug 2023) — confirmed via Guinness World Records. This is the **only sub-1:15 time in event history**.

**Recent winning/fastest times:**
| Year | Winner | Time |
|------|--------|------|
| 2018 | Neil Rutter | 1:18.81 (then WR) |
| 2023 | Neil Rutter | **1:12.35** (current WR) |
| 2024 | Sian Clement | ~1:29.33 (Rutter absent) |
| 2025 | Neil Rutter | 1:18.13 (6th title) |

**2025 next-fastest:** Thomas Howells 1:22.16, Lewis Purssey 1:26.50.

## Most decision-relevant insight for the 2026 <1:15.00 question
- **Sub-1:15 is essentially a Neil-Rutter-only phenomenon.** He's the only person ever to break 1:15, and even he usually wins in the ~1:18 range (1:18.81 in 2018, 1:18.13 in 2025). His record run of 1:12.35 in 2023 is an outlier.
- **When Rutter is absent (2024), the fastest time jumped to ~1:29.33** — the non-Rutter field consistently finishes above 1:22.
- **Rutter's 2026 participation is the dominant variable and is unconfirmed.** He retired after 2023, returned in 2025. The 2026 event is scheduled for Sunday 30 August 2026.

I've reframed the analysis around trajectory/distribution rather than predicting the outcome, and delivered full structured data with sources (Guinness World Records, Brecon & Radnor Express, Wikipedia).
